title: Capacity Constraints Make Admissions Processes Less Predictable
source_inventory_policy: Initial source-curated inventory from arXiv TeX source_tex/main.tex and source_tex/appendix.tex, with AAAI page as canonical publication metadata. Empirical private-data performance claims are tracked as descriptive/out-of-theorem-scope unless reduced to a formal choice-function proposition.

definition_q_acceptance.statement: Definition: a choice function is q-acceptant when it chooses exactly min(q, |X|) applicants from every finite input set X.
definition_q_acceptance.source_location: Main text Definition q-Acceptance / Appendix restatement

definition_total_order_and_queue.statement: Definition/prose: a total order is transitive, asymmetric, and complete; a q-acceptant choice function is characterized by a total order when it chooses the top-q elements of each set.
definition_total_order_and_queue.source_location: Main text Definition Total order and following queue prose

definition_choice_distance.statement: Definition: r_C(X1,X2) is |X1 ∩ C(X2) \ C(X1)| + |C(X1) \ C(X2)| for X1 subset X2.

definition_d_instability.statement: Definition: C is d-unstable when adding one applicant changes at most d existing decisions, measured by choice distance; tightly d-unstable means d-unstable but not (d-1)-unstable.

definition_variability.statement: Definition: for a 1-unstable q-acceptant choice function, variability is max_X | union over x' of C(X) \ C(X ∪ {x'}) |.

proposition_ml_representation.statement: Proposition: independent pointwise ML rules only represent 0-unstable choice functions; rank-threshold ML rules can represent 1-variable, 1-unstable choice functions and cannot represent instability or variability greater than one.

definition_substitutability.statement: Definition: C is substitutable when X1 subset X2 implies X1 ∩ C(X2) subset C(X1).
definition_substitutability.source_location: Main text Definition Substitutability / Appendix restatement

theorem_instability.statement: Theorem: for a q-acceptant choice function, it cannot be 0-unstable under the nontrivial-universe condition, it is exactly 1-unstable iff substitutable, and tightly d-unstable examples exist for every 1 <= d <= 2q.
theorem_instability.source_location: Main text Theorem Instability and appendix proof

definition_sequential_composition.statement: Definition: C is a sequential composition of C_n,...,C_1 when it chooses from each stage's remaining set and unions the chosen sets.
definition_sequential_composition.source_location: Main text Definition Sequential Composition / Appendix restatement

theorem_variability.statement: Theorem: a q-acceptant 1-unstable choice function represented as a sequential composition of n total-order queues has variability m with 1 <= m <= n, and variability 1 iff it is characterized by a single total order.
theorem_variability.source_location: Main text Theorem Variability and appendix proof

proposition_program_variability.statement: Proposition: the considered NYC program choice functions are 1-unstable, with tight variability equal to their number of queues: 1, 2, 3, and 6 for the listed program classes.

definition_monotonicity.statement: Definition: C is monotonic when X1 subset X2 implies C(X1) subset C(X2).

definition_consistency.statement: Definition: C is consistent when C(X2) subset X1 subset X2 implies C(X2) = C(X1).

definition_q_representativeness.statement: Definition: a q-acceptant choice function is q-representative when some strict total order makes C(X) the top q elements of X for all X.

lemma_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompat.statement: Lemma: if the universe has size greater than q and q >= 1, no choice function is both monotonic and q-acceptant.
lemma_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompat.source_location: Appendix Lemma Incompatibility of Monotonicity and q-Acceptance

lemma_unsubstitutable_single_add.statement: Lemma: if C is not substitutable, then some single added applicant x' causes a previously rejected existing applicant x* to become accepted.

lemma_substitutability_distance_term.statement: Lemma: C is substitutable iff |X1 ∩ C(X2) \ C(X1)| = 0 for all X1 subset X2.

lemma_monotonicity_distance_term.statement: Lemma: C is monotonic iff |C(X1) \ C(X2)| = 0 for all X1 subset X2.

theorem_choice_distance_triangle.statement: Theorem: choice distance satisfies the triangle inequality for X1 subset X2 subset X3.

definition_zero_instability.statement: Definition: C is 0-unstable iff r_C(X1,X2)=0 for all X1 subset X2.

corollary_zero_distance.statement: Corollary: C is 0-unstable iff it is both substitutable and monotonic.

definition_independence.statement: Definition: C is independent when every applicant is either always accepted whenever available or always rejected whenever available.

theorem_independent_substitutable_monoto.statement: Theorem: C is independent iff it is both substitutable and monotonic.
theorem_independent_substitutable_monoto.source_location: Appendix Theorem Independent Rules are Substitutable and Monotonic

corollary_independent_zero_unstable.statement: Corollary: C is 0-unstable iff it is independent; therefore no q-acceptant C is 0-unstable under the nontrivial-universe condition.
corollary_independent_zero_unstable.source_location: Appendix Corollary Only Independent Rules are 0-unstable

theorem_substitutability_one_instability.statement: Theorem: any q-acceptant choice function is 1-unstable iff substitutable.
theorem_substitutability_one_instability.source_location: Appendix Theorem Substitutability and 1-Instability are Equivalent Under Capacity Constraints

theorem_substitutable_q_acceptant_consis.statement: Theorem: any q-acceptant substitutable choice function is consistent.

lemma_calculating_instability.statement: Lemma: for q-acceptant C, X'=X∪{x'}, |X|>=q, and n=|C(X)\C(X')|, r_C(X,X') = 2n - 1_{x' in C(X')}.

theorem_even_instability_inconsistency.statement: Theorem: for q-acceptant C, C is inconsistent iff there exist X and X'=X∪{x'} with positive even choice distance.
theorem_even_instability_inconsistency.source_location: Appendix Theorem Even Instability is Inconsistent

corollary_no_consistent_even_instability.statement: Corollary: there is no q-acceptant consistent C that is tightly d-unstable for even d.
corollary_no_consistent_even_instability.source_location: Appendix Corollary No Consistent Tightly Even Instability

definition_general_variability.statement: Definition: general variability is the max of the largest borderline set V_C(X) and waitlisted set A_C(X).

theorem_append_remove_variability.statement: Theorem: for q-acceptant 1-unstable C and universe size at least 2q, the maximum waitlisted-set size equals the maximum borderline-set size.

lemma_corrected_consistency_of_removable.statement: Corrected lemma: if C is 1-unstable and q-acceptant and C(X1)=C(X2), then V_C(X1)=V_C(X2). The TeX source has the typo V_C(X1)=V_C(X1).
lemma_corrected_consistency_of_removable.source_location: Appendix Lemma Consistency of Removable Sets

lemma_ranking_m.statement: Lemma: for q-acceptant 1-unstable C with variability 1, V_C(X)=A_C(X∪{x'}) when adding x' changes the chosen set.

theorem_q_representative_variability.statement: Theorem: C is q-representative iff it is q-acceptant and 1-unstable with variability 1.
theorem_q_representative_variability.source_location: Appendix Theorem q-Representativeness and 1-Variability are Equivalent

theorem_sequential_composition_substitut.statement: Theorem: sequential composition of substitutable choice functions is substitutable.

theorem_additive_variability_bound.statement: Theorem: a sequential composition of q-acceptant 1-unstable functions with variabilities m1,...,mn has variability at most sum_i m_i.

lemma_lap_ordering.statement: Lemma: in a linear assignment problem, the applicant assigned to slot s is ordered above every rejected applicant by slot s's ordering.

theorem_lap_variability.statement: Theorem: the variability of a linear assignment problem is upper bounded by the number of distinct preference orderings induced by its slots.
